What we work on

Strategic communication is a leadership practice.

Work through an upcoming board presentation, a stakeholder conflict, a decision meeting or a leadership transition with a practical, candid partner.

  • Executive presence: pace, pauses, emphasis, fewer qualifiers
  • Bottom line up front: concise updates and recommendations
  • Presenting to boards and the C-suite; handling hostile questions
  • Disagreeing without losing authority
  • Panel interviews for Director and VP roles
  • Negotiating senior compensation and offers

It starts with a diagnostic

See exactly where you’re losing ground.

The first session puts your communication under realistic pressure, then scores it across clarity, conciseness, authority, structure, persuasion, diplomacy, spontaneity and cultural awareness.

  1. 90-second introduction

    Presence, structure and naturalness.

  2. A complex project, explained

    Clarity and adapting to the audience.

  3. A recommendation to leadership

    Conciseness and authority.

  4. Disagreeing with a senior stakeholder

    Diplomacy and confidence.

  5. An unexpected question

    Spontaneity and composure.

  6. Negotiating a deadline

    Persuasion and stakeholder management.
